TWO VIEWS OF THE ABDOMEN DATED ___

HISTORY:  ___ woman with Crohn disease and extensive bowel surgery,
now with abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and fever;? obstruction.

FINDINGS:  Two views are compared with the study dated ___.  There are
numerous gas-filled bowel loops throughout the central upper and lower
abdomen, predominantly colonic, with abundant retained stool.  There are also
a few gas-filled but normal caliber small bowel loops, particularly in the low
pelvis, and there are scattered fluid levels.  There is no free
subdiaphragmatic gas or unusual gas collection.  Noted are anastomotic ring
suture in the right mid abdomen, as well as numerous calcified injection
granulomata in both buttocks.

IMPRESSION:  Non-specific bowel gas pattern with fecoloaded colon.  No
pneumoperitoneum.

RIGHT UPPER QUADRANT ULTRASOUND ___.

HISTORY:  ___ woman with Crohn disease, s/p "extensive" abdominal
surgeries, now with nausea, vomiting and new fever, and "palpable mass" in
right upper quadrant.

FINDINGS:  Real-time sonography with color flow Doppler interrogation, limited
to the right upper abdomen, was performed in the Radiology Department, and
compared with the CTs dated ___ and ___.  There is no ascites.  The liver
appears diffusely and coarsely echogenic, most suggestive of generalized fatty
infiltration, although such a process  cannot be confirmed on either the ___
NECT or ___ CECT.  Allowing for this, there is no focal hepatic abnormality
or intrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation, and the CBD is normal in caliber,
measuring 5.1 mm in the porta hepatis.  The more distal CBD, as well as the
pancreas, itself, cannot be visualized due to substantial overlying bowel gas.
There is normal hepatopetal flow in the main portal vein.  Limited views of
the right kidney are grossly unremarkable.  The gallbladder is surgically
absent.

IMPRESSION:  Limited study (primarily due to the presence of abundant bowel
gas) in this patient, status post cholecystectomy.  However, no discrete
hepatic or other right upper abdominal mass is seen, and the proximal CBD is
normal in caliber.

Although the overall hepatic echogenicity is suggestive of diffuse fatty
infiltration (common in patients with Crohn disease), this is not supported by
the previous CT studies, and other processes, such as other infiltrative
disease or fibrosis should be considered.
